phases.name: Phase 1 - real-dependency smoke against the installed anthropic SDK

parallel_group.success_criteria: pyproject.toml declares an `anthropic` optional extra pinned `>=1,<2` CARRYING a `python_version >= '3.10'` environment marker, and includes the same marked entry in the `all` extra; a dependency resolution targeting Python 3.9 omits the SDK rather than failing; `agent-io/work-records/anthropic-sdk-smoke.md` exists and names, for the INSTALLED anthropic package, the async client class, the message-create method path, the four request parameter names, the usage attribute names for input/output/cache-creation/cache-read tokens, the content-block and stop-reason attribute names, the typed exception classes with how to read status code and parsed error body, how to read response headers, and the client's retry parameter name with its default value plus whether `_should_retry` inspects the parsed error code -- each marked as verified-by-inspection or explicitly unverified; the file states either the observed live-call result or that no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was available and the live call was skipped; it contains a `FIXTURE BASIS` section; `import kbutillib` still succeeds; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

parallel_group.prompt:
Write the `anthropic` LLM api type for KBUtilLib: a native POST /v1/messages backend using the official `anthropic` SDK.

READ FIRST: `agent-io/work-records/anthropic-sdk-smoke.md` on your base commit. It records the SDK's ACTUAL inspected attribute and parameter names and a `FIXTURE BASIS` section. Use it as the authority on SDK shape. Anything it marks unverified, verify yourself by inspecting the installed package -- do not guess, and do not take a name from this prompt over a name in that file.

READ ALSO: `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/llm/protocol.py` (the `ApiType` protocol and `REQUIRED_MEMBERS`), `llm/types.py` (`LLMRequest`, `LLMResult`, the typed failures and their `retryable`/`halts_endpoint` class vars, `LLMError.rate_limited`, `WEB_SEARCH_PARAM`), and `llm/apis/http_common.py` (for the conventions to mirror -- `redact`, `strip_fences`, `extract_json_object`, `strip_think`, the `transport=` test seat, and the never-raise guard in `complete`).

CREATE `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/llm/apis/anthropic.py` with one class `AnthropicBackend`:

- `kind = "anthropic"`; `supports_web_search = False`; `DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "https://api.anthropic.com"`.
- Constructed from ONE endpoint-config mapping, like `HttpBackend`: `{}` is valid and falls back to defaults. Read `base_url`, `api_key`, `api_key_env`, `timeout`, `proxy`, `extra_body`, `name`. Provide a test injection point for the HTTP transport so the full request path is exercisable with no socket, mirroring `HttpBackend`'s `transport=` parameter. NOTE: the SDK ships its own HTTP stack (httpx2), separate from the project's httpx -- the endpoint's `proxy` key must be wired to the SDK's client EXPLICITLY; it is not inherited.
- CONSTRUCT THE SDK CLIENT WITH RETRIES DISABLED (`max_retries=0`, but use the parameter name the phase-1 work record confirms), AND APPLY IT TO THE CLIENT USED BY `models()` AS WELL AS `complete()` -- if one-attempt-per-call is the house rule, a diagnostic enumeration does not get an exemption. THIS IS NOT A TUNING PREFERENCE. The SDK's `_should_retry` retries on HTTP status INCLUDING 429 without inspecting the parsed error body's error code, and the client default is 2 retries. Two consequences: (a) it breaks a STATED INVARIANT of this repository -- read the `llm/__init__.py` module docstring, which promises 'Exactly one attempt per call. Retries, backoff, budgets, halts, concurrency limits and single-flight collapsing belong to the caller (for the council, to CouncilWorker) because only the caller knows what a second attempt would cost' -- and makes CouncilWorker's own `max_attempts` a multiplier rather than a limit; (b) a spend-cap 429 can NEVER succeed, so two internal retries are two guaranteed-wasted requests per attempt, each consuming the per-minute allowance, which is how the engine's sustained-rate halt then fires and reports a RATE problem for an EMPTY WALLET. Add a comment at the construction site recording both reasons so nobody 'helpfully' re-enables it.
- IMPORT THE SDK LAZILY, inside the constructor or a helper -- never at module scope. A missing package must raise an error whose message names BOTH the extra (`pip install 'kbutillib[anthropic]'`) AND the Python >= 3.10 requirement. The Python requirement belongs in the message because the extra carries a `python_version >= '3.10'` marker, so on Python 3.9 the install silently resolves to NOTHING and 'install the extra' would be advice that cannot work. Follow the convention documented above the `backfill`/`pymongo` extra in `pyproject.toml`.
- Credential: an explicit `api_key`, else the variable named by `api_key_env` (default `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). UNLIKE the OpenAI-compatible backend, there is NO `"EMPTY"` fallback -- an absent credential returns an `AuthError`-shaped failure through the normal path. Pass the key EXPLICITLY to the SDK client; do not rely on the SDK's own environment resolution, or a run can silently use a different credential than the config declares. Never log, store or put the key in an error message; route anything that could quote it through `redact`.

REQUEST CONSTRUCTION:
- model <- `req.model` verbatim; the output-token ceiling <- `req.max_output_tokens` (this API REQUIRES it, so always send it); system <- `req.system` as the TOP-LEVEL system parameter, omitted when empty; messages <- a single user message carrying `req.user`.
- SEND A SAMPLING PARAMETER ONLY WHEN IT IS NOT None. Concretely: send `temperature` IFF `req.temperature is not None`, and likewise for any `top_p`/`top_k` arriving via `params`. This is load-bearing and is NOT a style choice: these parameters are REMOVED on the current Claude models (Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7) and return HTTP 400, while `SeatSpec.temperature` defaults to `0` -- so forwarding the field default the way `HttpBackend._params` does would fail EVERY call on EVERY current Claude model. The repository already records the same fact for the ARGO route in `ARGO_NO_TEMPERATURE_MODELS` in `llm/apis/http.py`.
  DO NOT instead test whether `req.params` carries a temperature. That reading is WRONG and was caught by a confront adversary that executed the real function: `CouncilConfig._seat` does `temperature = params.pop("temperature", 0)` (council/config.py:982), so an explicitly configured temperature is MOVED OUT of the model's params onto `SeatSpec.temperature` and `as_llm_request` copies that field separately. Measured: `params={'temperature': 0.3}` yields `seat.temperature=0.3` and `seat.extra={}`. A backend reading `params` therefore silently DROPS an explicit temperature, and one reading `req.temperature` unconditionally SENDS the default 0 -- two observably different wrong implementations.
  The None test works because a LATER PHASE changes `_seat` to set `temperature=None` for an `anthropic` seat whose model params omit temperature (phase `anthropic-config-and-literal`). Until that phase lands, an anthropic seat built through `_seat` still carries `0`; that is expected, and your tests must drive `LLMRequest` directly rather than depending on the config change. `LLMRequest.temperature`'s own docstring already defines `None` as 'do not send a temperature at all', so this uses the existing contract rather than inventing one. Do NOT introduce a per-model reject-list: a hardcoded list rots on the next model release.
- DO NOT send a `thinking` parameter; leave the provider default.
- DO NOT request structured outputs / `output_config.format`.
- Merge the endpoint's `extra_body` and the request's own `params` as provider extras, dropping the two keys that are not generation parameters: `extra_body` and `WEB_SEARCH_PARAM`. Mirror `HttpBackend._model_params`.
- GUARD THE EXTRAS, because a passthrough can defeat every invariant above. `model`, `messages` and `max_tokens` are RESERVED: an extra that would overwrite one is REFUSED, not silently merged (a caller who overwrites `model` has changed which model the route fingerprint claims). `stream` and `tools` are FORBIDDEN in this lane: both change the response shape this parse does not handle.
- REFUSE, before anything is sent, any request carrying `cache_control`. The check must be RECURSIVE over the MERGED request `params` and endpoint `extra_body` -- not a top-level key test, because a nested `cache_control` is exactly the one that would get through. Return `ok=False` with an `InvalidOutput`-kind error explaining that cache-aware billing is out of scope in v1. Reason: cache reads are billed at a fraction of base input, so passing them through would make the dollar figure disagree with the token figure.

RESPONSE PARSE:
- Content is a LIST OF BLOCKS. Concatenate the text of EVERY block whose type is `text`, in order. Do NOT index block 0 -- with thinking on, a non-text block legitimately comes first, and its text is empty by default.
- USAGE MAPPING -- THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS TASK. Emit a usage dict in the engine's vocabulary:
    prompt_tokens = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens   (each absent field read as 0)
    completion_tokens = output_tokens
  Write it as that SUM, not as the bare `input_tokens`, because `input_tokens` counts only tokens AFTER the last cache breakpoint. The engine's budget reads exactly `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` and sums them; a backend that passed Anthropic's own field names through would report ZERO spend, the budget ceiling would never trip and the halt would never fire. Leave `usage` as `None` ONLY when the provider reported no usage object at all -- that is how the engine tells "free" from "unmeasurable", and it must stay distinguishable.
- `resolved_model` <- the response's model field.
- Stop reason `max_tokens` -> return `ok=False`, `truncated=True`, with an `InvalidOutput`-kind error saying a cut-off answer is not a vote. Mirror the `finish_reason == "length"` branch in `HttpBackend._complete`. This API's vocabulary is `max_tokens`, NOT OpenAI's `length`.
- Stop reason `refusal` -> `ok=False`, `InvalidOutput`, not retryable, with the stop-details category in the message. Guard before reading stop details: they are populated only for a refusal.
- Clean the text before locating the JSON object, then use `extract_json_object`. The cleaner MUST strip BOTH `<think>...</think>` AND `<thinking>...</thinking>` -- the shared `strip_think` helper matches only the former, and this provider's documented tag-leakage uses the latter. Getting this wrong fails intermittently, on the subset of leaks containing a brace. WRITE AN ANTHROPIC-LOCAL CLEANER AND DO NOT MODIFY THE SHARED `strip_think` HELPER: it is called by ARGO and by every OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and widening it to fix a provider none of them use is how an unrelated route changes behaviour inside a PRD that never mentions it. Add a test asserting that ARGO/openai cleaning behaviour is byte-identical to the base commit.
- `schema_enforced = False` on every result -- no schema was requested of the provider and the engine validates the answer itself.

ERROR TAXONOMY -- map onto the existing typed failures in `llm/types.py`, in THIS order (the two spend-limit matches MUST come before the generic status rules):
  1. HTTP 400 whose error message begins, case-insensitively, `You have reached your specified API usage limits` -> `QuotaExhausted` (halts the endpoint). This is the OPERATOR-SET SPEND LIMIT and it is the most likely way this wallet empties. There is no machine-readable code on it, so match the documented message prefix and include the matched text in the error message so a future wording change shows up as a halt that stopped firing rather than a silent regression.
  2. HTTP 429 whose parsed error body carries error_code `enforced_spend_limit_reached` -> `QuotaExhausted` (halts the endpoint). This is the ORGANISATION MONTHLY SPEND CAP; it carries no `retry-after` and retrying it cannot succeed.
  3. HTTP 401 / 403 -> `AuthError` (halts the endpoint).
  4. HTTP 429 otherwise -> `TransportError` with `rate_limited=True` (retryable). Set that flag the way `HttpBackend._status_error` does -- the engine's sustained-rate halt counts flagged failures and must not count ordinary transport blips.
  5. HTTP >= 500 -> `TransportError` (retryable).
  6. Any other 4xx -> `InvalidOutput` (the request was wrong, not the credential).
  7. Connection failure -> `TransportError`; deadline exceeded -> `CallTimeout`.

ALSO IMPLEMENT:
- `effective_params(request)` -- deterministic, generation parameters ONLY, no credential/header/proxy/routing. It must report the ABSENCE of a temperature when none is sent, so the route fingerprint is honest about the omission.
- `complete(req)` -- NEVER raises for a call failure. Convert `req` via `as_llm_request` INSIDE the guard, so even a wrongly-shaped request returns a typed failure. Pass any escaping message through `redact`.
- `async preflight()` -- free, spends nothing: `ready` when the credential resolves, `refused` with a reason when it does not. Report the NAME of what was resolved, never the value.
- `async models()` -- list the provider's models; return `[]` on any failure, because enumeration is a diagnostic and never a precondition for a call.
- `async aclose()` -- release the SDK client.
- Read the `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-limit`, `-requests-remaining`, `-requests-reset` and the input/output token header families off each response and expose them on the instance as last-observed values, logged at debug. RECORD ONLY -- do not feed them into any pacing decision.

REGISTER IT in `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/llm/__init__.py`: add a `_make_anthropic` lazy factory next to the existing four, register it via `_register_builtin("anthropic", _make_anthropic)`, add `"anthropic"` to `BUILTIN_API_TYPES` (keeping that tuple sorted), and update the module docstring, which currently says four api types are built in and that a FIFTH would come from another distribution.

TESTS -- add a new test module. Build fixtures from the `FIXTURE BASIS` section of the phase-1 work record, NOT from prose. Table-driven over response envelopes: text only; a thinking block first then text; multiple text blocks; fenced JSON; `<thinking>` leakage; stop reason `max_tokens`; stop reason `refusal`; usage with all three input fields; usage with only input and output tokens; usage absent entirely. One case per error-taxonomy row above, asserting the resulting error kind, `retryable`, `halts_endpoint` and `rate_limited`. Two tests matter most and must be present:
  (a) a NEGATIVE test that a usage object carrying ONLY Anthropic's own field names still produces a NON-ZERO `prompt_tokens` under the key `prompt_tokens` -- a pass-through implementation must FAIL this test;
  (b) a test that calls the engine's OWN summing function, `kbutillib.domains.ai.council.engine.worker._token_total`, on the usage dict your backend produced and asserts a non-zero result -- import and call the real function rather than re-implementing the sum, so the test cannot drift from what the budget actually reads.
Also assert `effective_params` omits temperature by default and includes it only when explicitly set; that `import kbutillib` works with the SDK absent (simulate the absence; do not uninstall it) and that constructing the endpoint then errors naming both the extra and the Python requirement; and that THE CONSTRUCTED SDK CLIENT HAS RETRIES DISABLED -- assert it by inspecting the constructed client object's retry setting, NOT by reading the source line that sets it, so the test fails if a later refactor drops the argument. Add one further test that a single `complete()` call against a 429-returning transport results in EXACTLY ONE upstream request, which is the behavioural form of the same guarantee.

Assert on `LLMResult` and on published dicts -- never on private internals.
parallel_group.success_criteria: `llm.api_types()` includes `"anthropic"` and `llm.get_api("anthropic", {...})` returns an instance passing `llm.protocol.missing_members` with an empty list; `BUILTIN_API_TYPES` contains `"anthropic"`; a response envelope whose usage carries only `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` yields an `LLMResult` whose `usage["prompt_tokens"]` is non-zero AND for which the real `council.engine.worker._token_total` returns non-zero; a `stop_reason` of `max_tokens` yields `ok=False` with `truncated=True`; an HTTP 400 whose message begins `You have reached your specified API usage limits` and an HTTP 429 carrying `enforced_spend_limit_reached` each yield an error with `halts_endpoint=True` and kind `quota_exhausted`; a plain 429 yields a retryable error with `rate_limited=True`; a request carrying `cache_control` yields `ok=False` with nothing sent; `effective_params` contains no temperature key for a request that did not set one explicitly; `<thinking>` blocks are stripped before JSON extraction; `complete` returns a typed failure rather than raising for every failure case tested including a wrongly-shaped request; the CONSTRUCTED SDK client object has retries disabled, asserted by inspecting the client rather than the source, and a single `complete()` against a 429-returning transport produces exactly one upstream request; `import kbutillib` succeeds with the anthropic package absent and constructing the endpoint then errors naming both `kbutillib[anthropic]` and the Python >= 3.10 requirement; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

phases.name: Phase 3 - open the closed Literal and teach the council config about the kind

parallel_group.prompt:
Make the council able to SEAT an `anthropic` endpoint. The api type is registered by the previous phase, but a seat is still refused at roster construction by a closed type annotation. There is NO store migration in this task -- see the explicit note below.

EDIT `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/types.py`:
- Add `"anthropic"` to the `Literal[...]` on `SeatSpec.endpoint_kind`. THIS IS THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: the llm registry is open (entry points plus `register_api_type`) and `council.config._require_registered_kind` already asks `llm.api_types()` rather than any local list, so config load accepts the kind as soon as it is registered -- but `SeatSpec` pins `endpoint_kind` to six values and a seat on a seventh raises a pydantic ValidationError.
- Add `"anthropic"` to the `ENDPOINT_KINDS` tuple.
- DO NOT add it to `HTTP_KINDS`. That tuple currently means `("argo", "openai")`, i.e. OPENAI-SHAPED, not merely URL-reached. Adding `anthropic` because the endpoint has a URL would quietly tell every reader of that tuple that the request shape is OpenAI's. Before you leave this file, grep every reader of `HTTP_KINDS` and add a short comment next to the tuple recording that `anthropic` is URL-reached but deliberately excluded, and why.
- DO NOT TOUCH `council/store/schema.py`. The `endpoint_kind` column is `sa.String(32)` with NO CHECK constraint, so no migration is owed. Confirm this by reading the column and say so in the work record; do not write a migration.

EDIT `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/config.py`:
- `DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY["anthropic"] = 4`. Deliberately below the `openai` default of 16: on this provider the binding constraint is the per-minute REQUEST RATE, not the parallel cap, and a low cap with a correct pacer is safe while the reverse is how the 2026-10-21 MAG pilot errored 427 of 500 items. Comment it to that effect.
- In `EndpointConfig._check`, add an `anthropic` branch BEFORE the generic no-URL plug-in branch. It must default `base_url` to `https://api.anthropic.com` when absent. REASON, and put it in the comment: `anthropic` is not in `BASE_URL_KINDS`, so without this the endpoint falls down the branch that demands `reuse_namespace` and is refused for a reason about answer caching that an operator cannot guess from the message. Filling the default also gives `types.default_reuse_namespace` a real identity to derive a namespace from, which is what that branch was protecting.
- In the same branch, REFUSE `billing: subscription` for an `anthropic` endpoint with a `ConfigError` explaining that this is an API-billed wallet and the CLI kinds are the subscription path.
- In the same branch, REQUIRE `account` AND REQUIRE THAT IT EQUAL THE RESOLVED RATE-LIMIT BUCKET NAME for the endpoint's models. Refusing only the cross-bucket case leaves the opposite hole open, which a confront adversary found in the draft: two aliases for the SAME bucket carrying two different arbitrary `account` strings pass every other check and produce TWO INDEPENDENT PACERS against one provider allowance -- reproducing exactly the over-subscription this validation exists to prevent. Requiring `account == bucket` shuts that hole with no new config key, because two aliases on one bucket then necessarily share an account string.
- Also add the cross-endpoint validation: refuse a configuration in which two `anthropic` endpoints share an `account` while their models belong to DIFFERENT buckets, and refuse one `anthropic` endpoint whose models span two buckets.
- REFUSE AT LOAD a seated canonical model that has NO ENTRY in the rate-limit bucket table, naming the canonical identity and the configuration override that would supply it. The draft left this unspecified; an unknown model silently becoming its own bucket is the same over-subscription hole again.
- Add an OPTIONAL non-secret `billing_wallet` field to `EndpointConfig`, DEFAULTING TO `account` so every existing endpoint kind is unchanged byte for byte, and REQUIRED for an `anthropic` endpoint. It is consumed by a later phase (the quote's balance-delta block). It exists because once `account` names the rate-limit bucket, several Anthropic buckets sit on ONE API wallet with one console balance, and `account` can no longer stand in for the payer.
- CHANGE `_seat` SO THE TEMPERATURE DISTINCTION SURVIVES. For an `anthropic` endpoint ONLY: a model whose params OMIT `temperature` must yield `SeatSpec.temperature = None`, while an explicitly configured value -- INCLUDING an explicit `0` -- is preserved verbatim. Every other endpoint kind keeps today's `0` default unchanged. WHY: `_seat` currently does `temperature = params.pop("temperature", 0)` (around council/config.py:982), which moves an explicit temperature out of the model's params onto the seat, so no backend can distinguish 'explicitly 0' from 'never set'. The anthropic backend sends a sampling parameter iff it is not None, and `LLMRequest.temperature`'s own docstring already defines `None` as 'do not send a temperature at all' -- so this uses an existing contract rather than inventing one. Test all three cases SEPARATELY: omitted, explicit 0, explicit non-zero. An assertion that lumps the first two together is the bug.
  WHY THE ACCOUNT RULE IS A REFUSAL AND NOT A CONVENTION: `account` is read by BOTH `quote.py::_gateway_of` (it is the pricing bucket) and `engine/worker.py::_build_limits` (it is the shared-semaphore and shared-rate-bucket group). A wrong grouping therefore either collapses several genuinely separate provider allowances into one -- throttling the run to the slowest model's rate -- or splits one shared allowance into independent pools, which is the MAG failure. Neither announces itself; both are discovered by being billed or by being slow.
- Add a module-level RATE-LIMIT BUCKET table mapping canonical model identity to bucket name, which the validation above checks against. Anthropic enforces RPM/ITPM/OTPM PER MODEL-CLASS BUCKET, not per organisation: Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 each hold a separate allowance, while Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5 SHARE one bucket and Sonnet 4.6/4.5 share another. The table MUST be overridable from configuration -- a new Claude model must need a config change and not a code change.
- Add `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_BY_KIND["anthropic"]` mapping served model ids to canonical identities: `claude-haiku-4-5 -> anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`, `claude-sonnet-5 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6 -> anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, `claude-opus-5 -> anthropic/claude-opus-5`, `claude-opus-4-8 -> anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`. THE COLLISION WITH ARGO IS DELIBERATE AND MUST NOT BE AVOIDED: `DEFAULT_CANONICAL` already maps ARGO's `claudesonnet5` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` and `claudeopus5` to `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, so `Roster._check_independence` will REFUSE seating both as proposers. That refusal is the mechanism that stops two wallets presenting one model as two independent votes. Comment it so a future reader does not "fix" it. Do NOT add a per-wallet suffix to make both seatable.
- Add ONLY the model ids listed above. The live pricing and rate-limit documentation also lists an Opus 5.5, a Sonnet 5.5 and a Haiku 5.5, but their exact model ID STRINGS could not be obtained during design. DO NOT invent an id by pattern. `GET /v1/models` returns the live list and is free; if you add any model beyond the five above, obtain its id that way and say in the work record how you obtained it.

TESTS: a config declaring `kind: anthropic` with no `base_url` and no `reuse_namespace` loads, and its resolved reuse namespace is NON-EMPTY and derived from the normalised base_url plus deployment_revision. DO NOT assert that it is DISTINCT from other endpoints' namespaces -- a confront adversary executed `default_reuse_namespace` for a haiku and an opus anthropic alias and got `https://api.anthropic.com#` for BOTH, and that sharing is DELIBERATE (aliases of one deployment may reuse answers; distinct canonical models stay separate in the reuse key regardless). An earlier draft of this PRD demanded per-alias uniqueness; that criterion was wrong and was withdrawn.
Further tests: `billing: subscription` is refused; a missing `account` is refused; an `account` that is not the resolved bucket name is refused; a seated canonical model absent from the bucket table is refused naming the canonical identity; a missing `billing_wallet` on an anthropic endpoint is refused while a non-anthropic endpoint defaults it to `account`; two aliases sharing an `account` across two different rate-limit buckets are refused with a message naming both buckets; two aliases sharing a bucket AND an `account` are accepted; `_seat` yields `temperature=None` for an anthropic model omitting temperature, `0` for one explicitly setting 0, the value for one setting non-zero, and still `0` for a NON-anthropic model omitting it; a `SeatSpec` with `endpoint_kind="anthropic"` constructs; and a `Roster` seating ARGO `claudesonnet5` and Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5` as two proposers raises `RosterError`. That last test asserts a REFUSAL is preserved -- label it clearly as such in a comment, because it is the only guard against a future change silently making the collision seatable.

ALSO add a test over the EXISTING `CouncilWorker._build_limits` using the new config: three `anthropic` aliases on three different accounts produce three distinct `_AccountLimit` objects; two aliases on one account share one object, with capacity equal to the minimum declared `max_concurrency` and pacer rate equal to the minimum declared `max_requests_per_minute`. Do not modify `_build_limits` -- this asserts the reuse claim rather than trusting it.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A `SeatSpec` with `endpoint_kind="anthropic"` constructs without error and `ENDPOINT_KINDS` contains `"anthropic"` while `HTTP_KINDS` does NOT; `council/store/schema.py` is unchanged and no migration file was added; a council config with `kind: anthropic` and neither `base_url` nor `reuse_namespace` loads successfully and yields a non-empty reuse namespace distinct from other endpoints'; `billing: subscription` on an `anthropic` endpoint raises `ConfigError`; a missing `account` raises `ConfigError`; two `anthropic` endpoints sharing one `account` whose models are in different rate-limit buckets raise `ConfigError` naming both buckets, while two sharing a bucket and an account load; `DEFAULT_CANONICAL_BY_KIND["anthropic"]` resolves `claude-sonnet-5` to the same canonical string `DEFAULT_CANONICAL` gives ARGO's `claudesonnet5`, and a `Roster` seating both as proposers raises `RosterError`; the rate-limit bucket table is overridable from configuration, demonstrated by a test; `_build_limits` tests show three accounts produce three `_AccountLimit`s and two aliases on one account share one with min capacity and min rate; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

phases.name: Phase 4 - fail loudly when the credential is missing

parallel_group.prompt:
Make a council run REFUSE at submit time when an `anthropic` seat has no API key, instead of letting the seats report unavailable and the calls park.

EDIT `src/kbutillib/domains/genome/ontology_mapping/council_run.py`, function `resolve_credentials`. Read it first, in full. It branches on `kind == "argo"`, then `kind == "openai"`, then falls through to a row reporting `"requires": "interactive_subscription_login" if kind in ("claude_cli", "codex_cli") else "none"`. An `anthropic` endpoint therefore lands on `"none"` -- reporting that a seat which CANNOT work without an API key needs no credential at all. That is the defect this task fixes.

Add an `anthropic` branch, modelled closely on the EXISTING `argo` branch, which is the right precedent because it RAISES rather than reporting a soft row:
- Resolve the variable named by the endpoint's `api_key_env`, defaulting to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- If an explicit `api_key` is set in the endpoint config, report a row with `"requires": "api_key"`, `"name": "api_key"`, `"source": "config"` -- mirroring how the `openai` branch handles that case.
- If the variable is set and non-empty, report `"requires": "api_key"`, `"name": <the variable name>`, `"source": "environment"`.
- If neither, raise `RunRefused` with a check name of `anthropic_api_key` and an ACTIONABLE message: name the endpoint, name the variable that is unset, say that an Anthropic seat cannot authenticate without it, say that a run started without it does not fail loudly -- the seats report unavailable and the calls park -- and give the exact export command to fix it. Match the tone and completeness of the existing `argo_user` refusal message.
- There is NO file fallback. The `openai` branch falls back to a token file because that is where the AmSC token lives; nothing equivalent exists for this provider, and inventing a path would be a guess.
- NEVER put the credential's VALUE in a returned row, in the exception message, or in a log line. The whole function's contract is that it reports the NAME of what was resolved and where it came from. Re-read the function's docstring and extend it to document the new branch in the same style as the others.

TESTS: an `anthropic` endpoint with its `api_key_env` variable set reports `requires: api_key` naming the variable with source `environment`, and the returned rows contain the value NOWHERE (assert on the serialised rows, not just on one field); an endpoint with an explicit `api_key` in config reports source `config`; an endpoint with neither raises `RunRefused` whose message names both the endpoint and the variable. Use an injected environment mapping -- the function takes one -- rather than mutating the real process environment.
parallel_group.success_criteria: `resolve_credentials` returns a row with `requires` equal to `api_key` for an `anthropic` endpoint whose credential resolves, naming the environment variable and not its value, with the value absent from the serialised rows entirely; it reports source `config` for an explicit `api_key` and source `environment` for a variable; it raises `RunRefused` naming the endpoint and the variable when neither is present; the function's docstring documents the `anthropic` branch alongside the existing ones; no `anthropic` endpoint can reach the `requires: none` fallthrough; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

phases.name: Phase 5 - price per model so the quote is exact by construction

parallel_group.prompt:
Make the council's dollar quote exact when one gateway carries several models at different prices.

READ FIRST: `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/quote.py` -- `_gateway_of`, `_price_gateways`, the `QuoteLine` model, and `_balance_delta_block`. Also `council/config.py::RateConfig`.

THE PROBLEM. `_price_gateways` buckets every line by `line.gateway` and looks up ONE `RateConfig` per gateway, with one `input_per_mtok` and one `output_per_mtok`. `_gateway_of` returns the endpoint's `account`, so a gateway can legitimately carry several models: Anthropic's rate-limit buckets group Opus 4.8 with Opus 4.7, and the `account` key must name the rate-limit bucket because the same key also groups the engine's semaphore and rate pacer. Today every Anthropic rate-limit bucket happens to hold models at one list price, so one rate per gateway is exact BY COINCIDENCE. A quote that is right by coincidence cannot be told apart from one that is right by construction -- until it silently is not, which on a fixed $200 wallet is expensive.

THE SCOPE IS THREE FUNCTIONS, NOT ONE. An earlier draft of this PRD said the change was 'confined to one function'; that was WRONG and a confront adversary demonstrated why by reading the publisher. `Quote.to_dict` selects priced gateways BY TRUTHINESS (`priced = [g for g in self.gateways if g.get("priced")]`, and `"dollars_complete": not unpriced`, around quote.py:1128-1160) and the quote CLI does the same (`if not gateway.get("priced")`, interfaces/cli/council.py:337). So a tri-state `priced: "partial"` -- which the draft proposed -- is a NON-EMPTY STRING, lands in the PRICED list, stays out of the unpriced list, and leaves `dollars_complete` reading TRUE over a partial subtotal. That is precisely the silent mispricing this module exists to refuse, introduced by its own fix. You must not reintroduce it.

THE CHANGE:
- Sub-bucket each gateway's lines by `line.canonical_model`. That field ALREADY EXISTS on `QuoteLine` -- add no new field.
- Resolve each sub-bucket's rate as `rates["<gateway>/<canonical_model>"]`, falling back to `rates["<gateway>"]`. `CouncilConfig.rates` is `Dict[str, RateConfig]` keyed by a free string, so the composite key needs NO schema change -- do not change `RateConfig`.
- The gateway entry keeps every field it publishes today, so existing readers do not break, and gains a `by_model` breakdown: per canonical model, its token totals, its resolved rate or `None`, and its dollar figures. `dollars_point` and `dollars_upper` become the SUM over sub-buckets.
- PRICING HONESTY, which is the point of this task:
  * every sub-bucket priced -> `priced: true`, exactly as today;
  * no sub-bucket priced -> `priced: false` with the existing `unpriced_reason` text unchanged;
  * SOME priced -> `priced: false` (KEEP IT A STRICT BOOLEAN) PLUS a new `partially_priced: true`, an `unpriced_models` list naming the models with no rate, a `dollars_known_subtotal`, and an `unpriced_reason` saying the subtotal covers only part of the tokens. Keeping `priced` false makes EVERY existing truthiness reader -- including any neither this prompt nor you have found -- treat a partial gateway as UNPRICED, which UNDERSTATES rather than overstates, and `dollars_complete` goes false on its own with no change. Fixing N readers to test `is True` makes the Nth one you miss overstate; failing safe makes it understate. That asymmetry is the whole reason for this shape. A partial sum MUST NEVER be presented as a total -- the same error as substituting a vendor list rate for an unknown one, which this module already refuses on measured grounds. Read the `_price_gateways` docstring and keep its reasoning intact and extended, not replaced.
  * a MULTI-RATE gateway publishes `rate: null` and `rate_provenance: null`, with the contributing rate and provenance records under `by_model`. One legacy rate pair cannot represent three rates, and picking one would misattribute provenance -- which `RateConfig` makes REQUIRED precisely so that no dollar figure is unlabelled.
  * a quote whose contributing rates are NOT ALL ONE CURRENCY is REFUSED, not summed. `RateConfig.currency` is a free string, so mixed denominations would otherwise be added together silently.
  * sum per-model costs UNROUNDED and round once at the gateway, so the `by_model` figures and the gateway total cannot disagree by rounding.
  * the existing `is_floor` warning fires if ANY contributing rate is marked a floor, naming which.
  * every existing warning string that a caller may match on should keep working; add warnings rather than rewording old ones.
- UPDATE `Quote.to_dict` to SURFACE the partial state: publish the known subtotal for a partially-priced gateway so an operator can see it. `dollars_complete` needs no change -- it is `not unpriced` and a partial gateway is already in that list via the boolean. These edits are additive presentation, not load-bearing correctness, precisely because the boolean fails safe.
- UPDATE THE QUOTE CLI (`src/kbutillib/interfaces/cli/council.py`) so a partially-priced gateway NAMES ITS UNPRICED CANONICAL MODELS rather than printing simply 'unpriced'. An operator needs to learn WHICH rate is missing.
- RE-KEY `_balance_delta_block` ON `billing_wallet` (the field added in the config phase), NOT on gateway. Aggregate the member gateways' token totals and NAME the member gateways in the row. WHY THIS CHANGED: the draft kept it on gateway and justified it with 'there is one balance per wallet' -- a sentence that was true before `account` came to mean the rate-limit bucket and false after. Keyed on gateway it emits one row per BUCKET, i.e. three rows asking a human for the SAME console balance, and an operator who copies the wallet delta into each attributes the whole bill three times and corrupts every per-bucket calibration derived from it.
  AND DO NOT DERIVE PER-MODEL RATES FROM ONE WALLET OBSERVATION. A single balance delta cannot be decomposed into three models' four rates. Add a comment and a line of documentation saying so, because the next person to read the block will otherwise do the division and write three confident wrong rates into `ai_council.rates`.

TESTS -- AND ASSERT ON THE PUBLISHED QUOTE AND THE CLI OUTPUT, NOT ONLY ON `_price_gateways`, because the defect described above lived entirely in the gap between them. A gateway with three canonical models and three composite rates prices each separately and the per-model figures sum to the gateway total; a composite key is preferred over the gateway fallback when both exist; a gateway-level rate still prices every model when no composite key is present (backwards compatibility); a gateway with rates for only some models reports `priced: false` with `partially_priced: true`, names exactly the unpriced ones, and publishes a subtotal equal to the sum over only the priced ones -- AND `to_dict()` lists that gateway under `unpriced_gateways` with `dollars_complete` FALSE, AND the CLI names the unpriced canonical model; a gateway with no rate at all is unchanged from today's `unpriced` behaviour, asserted against the existing expected shape; a multi-rate gateway publishes `rate: null` and `rate_provenance: null`; a quote mixing currencies is refused; per-model costs sum unrounded so `by_model` and the gateway total agree exactly; `is_floor` propagates from any single contributor; a line with `gateway=None` is still skipped; and three endpoints on three buckets sharing one `billing_wallet` produce exactly ONE balance-delta row naming all three member gateways.
parallel_group.success_criteria: `_price_gateways` prices each canonical model within a gateway at its own configured rate, preferring a `"<gateway>/<canonical_model>"` key over a `"<gateway>"` key and falling back to the gateway key when no composite key exists; each gateway entry carries a `by_model` breakdown whose dollar figures sum exactly to the entry's totals, summed unrounded and rounded once; `priced` remains a STRICT BOOLEAN and a partially-priced gateway reports `priced: false` with `partially_priced: true`, an `unpriced_models` list naming exactly the unpriced ones, and a `dollars_known_subtotal` covering only the priced tokens; the PUBLISHED `to_dict()` output lists that gateway under `unpriced_gateways` with `dollars_complete` false, and the quote CLI names its unpriced canonical models; a multi-rate gateway publishes `rate: null` and `rate_provenance: null`; a quote whose contributing rates mix currencies is refused rather than summed; a gateway with no configured rate produces the same `priced: false` entry and `unpriced_reason` as on the base commit; `is_floor` warnings fire when any contributing rate is a floor; `RateConfig` and `QuoteLine` are unchanged; `_balance_delta_block` is keyed on `billing_wallet` so three endpoints on three buckets sharing one wallet yield exactly one row naming all three member gateways, and it derives no per-model rates from that single observation; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

phases.name: Phase 6 - packaged config example and operator documentation

parallel_group.prompt:
Document the `anthropic` api type for an operator who has an API key and a fixed credit, and ship a commented configuration example.

EDIT `src/kbutillib/domains/ai/council/default_config.yaml`. Follow the precedent set by the existing `mag` block: a COMMENTED-OUT example that shows the shape without shipping live model ids or a credential. Read the `mag` and `my-vllm` blocks first and match their voice and level of detail. The example must show:
- one alias PER ANTHROPIC RATE-LIMIT BUCKET, not one per wallet and not one per model;
- on each: `kind: anthropic`, `api_key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `billing: api`, its own `account`, its own `max_concurrency` and its own `max_requests_per_minute`;
- no `base_url`, with a comment saying it defaults to `https://api.anthropic.com`;
- matching `models:` entries, with a note that a newly released Claude model is added HERE and needs no code change, and that `GET /v1/models` is free and returns the live list.

The prose around it must state, briefly and in the config file's own register:
- THE ACCOUNT KEY NAMES THE RATE-LIMIT BUCKET, NOT THE WALLET, and why: Anthropic enforces RPM/ITPM/OTPM per model-class bucket, so Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 each hold a separate allowance while Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5 share one and Sonnet 4.6/4.5 share another. The same `account` key groups the engine's semaphore and rate pacer AND buckets the dollar quote, so naming it after the wallet would throttle the run to the slowest model's rate, and naming it per model would split one shared allowance into independent pools -- which is how the 2026-10-21 MAG pilot errored 427 of 500 items.
- THE PER-MINUTE RATE BINDS BEFORE THE PARALLEL CAP on this provider, which is why `max_requests_per_minute` is the number to set and `max_concurrency` defaults low.
- `max_total_tokens` IS PER ENDPOINT. Several aliases mean several budgets, and NOTHING SUMS THEM -- a single fixed wallet is not expressible as one enforced ceiling today. Say this plainly; it is the sharpest limitation of this configuration and an operator who does not know it will believe they are protected when they are not.
- AN `anthropic` SEAT'S `max_output_tokens` MUST COVER THINKING PLUS THE ANSWER. Thinking is on by default and adaptive on the current Claude models, its tokens are billed and counted as OUTPUT, and the seat default of 4000 is frequently not enough -- a truncated answer is a wasted call. `effort` can be passed through as a seat parameter to trade depth against spend; this file should not choose a value.
- NO SAMPLING PARAMETER IS SENT BY DEFAULT, because the current Claude models reject `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` with HTTP 400. A seat on a model that accepts them can set one explicitly in its `params`, and should know the provider default is 1.0, not 0.
- THIS CREDIT IS A SECOND WALLET AT THE SAME PRICE, NOT A DISCOUNT. ARGO was measured billing Claude at vendor list within 1.5% on the 2026-10-20 bill. What it buys is independence from the ARGO cap and access to models ARGO does not serve -- not a saving.
- ARGO ALREADY SERVES SONNET 5 AND OPUS 5 under the SAME canonical identity, so a roster cannot seat both routes for one model: `Roster._check_independence` refuses it, deliberately, because that is what stops one model being counted as two votes. The models this wallet newly makes seatable are Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6.
- `rates` CAN BE KEYED PER MODEL as `"<account>/<canonical-model>"`, falling back to `"<account>"`, and every rate must carry a `provenance`. Note that `Claude Haiku 5.5` has input pricing TIERED BY PROMPT SIZE, which `RateConfig`'s single `input_per_mtok` cannot express -- do not declare a rate for it and expect an exact quote.

ALSO: find where the council's operator-facing documentation lives (there is an operator runbook under `agent-io/docs/`; check for a docs tree under `docs/` as well) and add an `anthropic` section covering the same ground plus: the install extra `pip install 'kbutillib[anthropic]'`; that the credential goes through `api_key_env` and nowhere else; how to verify an endpoint with a free preflight before committing money; and HOW TO MEASURE THE REAL RATE LIMITS -- make one call and read `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-limit` and the input/output token limit headers off the response, then compare against the configured `max_requests_per_minute`. Note that the reported limits are the most restrictive currently in effect (a workspace limit can shadow the model's) and that remaining counts are rounded to the nearest thousand, so they are a sanity check and not a control input.

Finally, document the three MONEY SIGNALS and what each does, because they look alike and behave differently: an ordinary HTTP 429 with a `retry-after` is retried and a sustained run of them halts the endpoint; an HTTP 429 carrying `enforced_spend_limit_reached` is the ORGANISATION MONTHLY CAP and halts immediately; and an HTTP 400 beginning `You have reached your specified API usage limits` is an OPERATOR-SET SPEND LIMIT and also halts immediately. The third is the most likely way a fixed credit runs out, because fencing a $200 credit with a $200 console limit is the obvious thing to do.

Add no new code in this task beyond what documentation needs. Do not change any default value.
parallel_group.success_criteria: `default_config.yaml` carries a commented `anthropic` example showing one alias per rate-limit bucket with `kind`, `api_key_env`, `billing: api`, its own `account`, `max_concurrency` and `max_requests_per_minute`, and no `base_url`; its prose states that `account` names the rate-limit bucket rather than the wallet and why, that the per-minute rate binds before the parallel cap, that `max_total_tokens` is per endpoint and nothing sums several budgets, that `max_output_tokens` must cover thinking plus answer, that no sampling parameter is sent by default, that the credit is a second wallet at the same price rather than a discount, that ARGO already serves Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 under the same canonical identity so both routes cannot be seated for one model, and that rates may be keyed per model; operator documentation gains an `anthropic` section covering the install extra, the credential channel, the free preflight, how to read the rate-limit response headers and compare them against the configured rate, and the three distinct money signals with the behaviour of each; the packaged config still loads successfully and every declared default is unchanged from the base commit; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.

parallel_group.prompt:
Write the acceptance rehearsal for this PRD: a single operator-run script that exercises a LIVE Anthropic endpoint and checks the criteria no stub can satisfy. This is the task that decides whether the PRD is actually finished, as opposed to having all its code merged.

WHY THIS EXISTS. The measured failure pattern on this project is a PRD sitting at `done` with an acceptance step nobody ran. Worse, the specific defect this PRD guards against -- a backend that reports zero token spend because the provider names its token counts differently -- is INVISIBLE to any test built on a fixture, because a fixture written from the same documentation as the code confirms the documentation rather than the API. So the usage assertion has to be made against a real call or it is not made at all.

FOLLOW THE EXISTING PRECEDENT: read `scripts/council/acceptance_rehearsal.py` and match its structure, its reporting format and its output conventions. Do not invent a second convention. Write the new script beside it under `scripts/council/`.

THE SCRIPT MUST:
- Require an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and REFUSE TO RUN without one, with a clear message. It must never fall back to a fixture, a stub or a recorded response -- a rehearsal that quietly passes offline is worse than no rehearsal, because it reports success for a check that did not happen.
- Print its estimated cost before doing anything and require explicit confirmation (an argument or an environment variable) before spending. The whole wallet is $200 and the rehearsal must not be a surprise charge.
- Make ONE real call per seated model, with a small prompt and a small output ceiling, and then CHECK AND REPORT, one line per check, pass or fail with the observed value quoted:
  1. the stored council call row for each call carries a NON-ZERO `prompt_tokens` and a non-zero `completion_tokens`. Read it OUT OF THE STORE, not off the in-memory result and not from a log line -- the store is what the budget and every later reader actually see.
  2. `council.engine.worker._token_total` called on that stored usage returns non-zero. Import and call the real function.
  3. the observed `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-limit` header value, printed, and compared against the endpoint's configured `max_requests_per_minute`, reporting a MISMATCH as a finding rather than a failure (the header reports the most restrictive limit currently in effect, which may legitimately be a workspace limit).
  4. a free preflight against each endpoint reports `ready`.
  5. a quote over the rehearsal roster reports one gateway row per rate-limit bucket, with a separate dollar figure for each, and the per-model `by_model` figures summing to each gateway total. Where a rate is not configured, assert the row says `unpriced` or `partial` rather than presenting a number.
  6. an endpoint configured with a deliberately tiny `max_total_tokens` halts with `budget_exhausted` after the budget is passed, and the halt reason quotes the spend and the budget. This is the check that proves the budget ceiling actually bites -- it is the whole reason check 1 matters.

DO NOT ATTEMPT A LIVE 'NO USAGE OBJECT' CHECK. PRD acceptance criterion 4 (an endpoint whose provider reports no usage object halts with `budget_usage_unknown`) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this script: there is no supported way to make the real Anthropic API omit its usage object, so a live form of that criterion could never be met. It belongs instead as an ENGINE INTEGRATION TEST with an INJECTED response whose usage is absent -- add that test under the normal test tree in this task, separate from the rehearsal script, and say in the work record that it is the offline counterpart of AC4.
- Write a machine-readable result file and a human-readable summary under `agent-io/reports/`, named with the date, following the naming and format of the existing rehearsal reports in that directory.
- NOT require a GPU, a pod, or any BERDL or lakehouse transport. It must run anywhere a key and a council store exist.

ALSO write `agent-io/work-records/anthropic-acceptance-rehearsal.md` documenting how to run it, what each check proves, its approximate cost, and -- explicitly -- which of the PRD's acceptance criteria it does NOT cover and why, so the gap is visible rather than assumed closed.

The script itself is the deliverable; you are NOT expected to have run it against a live key, and you must not claim to have done so. If no key is available to you, say so plainly in the work record and leave the live run to the operator.

STATE THE DELIVERY STATE EXPLICITLY. PRD criteria 1, 2, 3 and 6 are LIVE-ONLY and no autonomous build can close them: they need a credential, the models to call, an isolated council store and an explicit spending cap, all supplied by a human. So the work record must record the PRD as LIVE-ACCEPTANCE-PENDING, list exactly which criteria are pending and what the operator must supply for each, and must NOT claim acceptance. The measured failure this guards against is a PRD sitting at `done` with an acceptance step nobody ran -- which has happened on this fleet before and is the reason this phase exists at all.

For check 3, note that the rate-limit header observation is PROCESS-LOCAL: a backend attribute does not cross the process boundary into a queue worker's submitter, and if debug logging is off it is written nowhere. Read it from the call THIS SCRIPT makes, which is the one context where it is guaranteed to be in scope, and say so in the work record rather than implying the value is available generally.
parallel_group.success_criteria: A new rehearsal script exists under `scripts/council/` following the structure and reporting conventions of the existing `acceptance_rehearsal.py`; it refuses to run without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and never substitutes a fixture or recorded response; it requires explicit confirmation before spending and prints an estimated cost first; it implements and individually reports all six named checks, reading token usage out of the council store rather than from an in-memory result or a log line and calling the real `council.engine.worker._token_total`; it writes both a machine-readable and a human-readable report under `agent-io/reports/`; it needs no GPU, pod or lakehouse transport; `agent-io/work-records/anthropic-acceptance-rehearsal.md` documents how to run it, what each check proves, its approximate cost, and which PRD acceptance criteria it does not cover; the work record states plainly whether a live run was performed and does not claim one that did not happen; and no test that passed on the base commit fails.
